title: Policy state-machine de-synchronization causing stale fallback decisions and cross-region reroute loops
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:34 UTC we observed a capacity/regression incident where requests started being routed repeatedly between two regions and occasionally to incompatible model variants. Symptoms included elevated 5xx errors, large latency spikes for affected customers, and unit-cost increases due to retry storms. Root cause analysis shows a de-synchronization between the policy control plane and edge routing proxies: a partial policy rollout updated a preference pointer (preferred_region + variant_version) while some proxies retained the old policy version due to a TTL/refresh race. The routing fallback logic uses a cached policy lease and an asynchronous refresh; stale leases could point to a variant that is not compatible with the selected runtime (e.g., quantized variant on legacy kernel), causing immediate downstream failures and triggering the policy fallback path. Because the fallback also updated the policy weight in some cases, this created an oscillation loop across regions that amplified into a cross-region reroute storm.
timeline: 2026-03-09 22:34 UTC - First alert: spike in route latency and 5xxs. 2026-03-09 22:36 - Automated retry subsystem escalated traffic to alternate regions. 2026-03-09 22:40 - On-call triggered incident channel. 2026-03-09 22:52 - Mitigation: temporary global routing pin to region-us-west-2 applied. 2026-03-09 23:30 - Traffic normalized. 2026-03-10 - Post-incident investigation started.
root_cause: Race between policy rollout and proxy cache refresh. Policy control plane incremented policy_version and updated preferred_region+variant_version atomically, but proxies with stale leases applied an inconsistent decision graph. The fallback decision path was not idempotent and could mutate routing weights, creating feedback that led to oscillation. Additional contributing factor: absence of a monotonic policy version check and no lease-based pin for in-flight requests.
impact_summary: Affected hosted API customers experienced increased 5xx rates and latency for ~56 minutes. Several mid-market customers saw request failures causing feature regressions. Billing showed a ~12% token cost increase for the affected window due to retries and cross-region hops.
mitigations_and_action_items: 1) Short-term: Implement emergency circuit-breaker in routing proxies to stop weight mutations during detected oscillation windows (owner: Marco Reyes, due: 2026-03-15). 2) Add monotonic policy_version check in routing decision: reject policy application if proxy observes lower version than in-flight header and force full sync (owner: SRE team / Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-22). 3) Convert fallback path to pure read-only decision; mutation of policy weights moved to control plane via queued proposals (owner: Routing team / Marco Reyes, due: 2026-03-26). 4) Adopt lease-based cache semantics with min-lease window for pinned in-flight requests to avoid mid-request policy flips (owner: Runtime infra / Elena Martin, due: 2026-04-02). 5) Add chaos test to CI that simulates staggered policy rollout across 30% of proxies to catch de-synchronization (owner: Test Engineering / Samir Patel, due: 2026-04-09). 6) Improve alerts: create metric for policy_version divergence count and routing-oscillation rate (owner: Observability / Jin Park, due: 2026-03-19). 7) Postmortem doc and customer comms: draft to be shared with affected customers and CS (owner: Aisha Kapoor, due: 2026-03-14).
acceptance_criteria: - Routing proxies must reject applying out-of-order policy versions and log divergence events. - Fallback path must be read-only for routing decisions in prod; any weight changes require control-plane proposal PR. - Chaos test reproduces the earlier oscillation and the new guards prevent it. - New divergence and oscillation alarms fire within the expected thresholds and have runbooks attached.
runbook_changes: Added a new section: 'Detecting policy-version divergence' with steps to pin traffic, disable fallback mutators, and roll back policy rollout. Runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Routing+Runbook
